title: Coherent formal modules on an affine Noetherian scheme are finite modules over the completion
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/I^n$ the $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\mathcal I=\widetilde I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals associated to $I$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]; for an $A^\wedge$-module $M$ write $I^nM$ for $(IA^\wedge)^nM$ (the $A$-submodule generated by the $am$, $a\in I^n$). (1) Let $(\mathcal F_n)$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] and $M=\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_n)$ (limit along the maps induced by the transition maps), an $A^\wedge$-module by $(a_n)_n\cdot(x_n)_n=(a_nx_n)_n$ ($a_n\in A/I^n$ acts on $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_n)$ since $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$). Then $M$ is a finitely generated $A^\wedge$-module, and for every $n\ge1$ the projection $p_n:M\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_n)$ is surjective with kernel $I^nM$. (2) The functor $E:(\mathcal F_n)\mapsto\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_n)$, $(\alpha_n)\mapsto\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\alpha_n)$, is an equivalence of categories from $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ onto the category of finitely generated $A^\wedge$-modules and $A^\wedge$-linear maps; a quasi-inverse sends $M$ to $\big((M/I^nM)^\sim\big)_{n\ge1}$ with the canonical surjections as transition maps.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine, line 6272) and its proof (the explicit form (1) is what the proof establishes: M = lim M_n finite over A^ with M/I^nM = M_n, via Nakayama Algebra 00DV, Mittag-Leffler Homology 02N1 and the coherent/finite-module correspondence Lemma 01XZ)

proof.text: (From sheaves to modules.) $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] (the affine covering by $X$ itself, $\mathcal O_X(X)=A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]). Write $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A,I}$ for the category of inverse systems $(M_n)_{n\ge1}$ of finitely generated $A$-modules with $I^nM_n=0$ whose transition map induces an isomorphism $M_{n+1}/I^nM_{n+1}\cong M_n$, with morphisms the compatible families of $A$-linear maps. Let $(\mathcal F_n)$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] and $M_n=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_n)$. Each $\mathcal F_n$ is coherent, hence quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so $M_n$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a). The ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\widetilde I$ has $\mathcal I(X)=I$ (the unit $\tau_X$ is an isomorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (2)), so by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2), for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal G$, $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal G)(X)=I^n\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$ and $\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G)$ is surjective with kernel $I^n\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$. Hence $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$ gives $I^nM_n=0$, and applying $\Gamma(X,-)$ to the isomorphism $\mathcal F_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}\cong\mathcal F_n$ gives that $\Gamma$ of the transition map induces $M_{n+1}/I^nM_{n+1}\cong M_n$. So $\Gamma_\bullet:(\mathcal F_n)\mapsto(\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_n))$, $(\alpha_n)\mapsto(\Gamma(X,\alpha_n))$ is a functor $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A,I}$, and $E=\varprojlim\circ\,\Gamma_\bullet$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine), first sentences: 'By the correspondence between coherent sheaves on X and finite A-modules (Lemma 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian) it suffices to show Mod^fg_{A,I} is equivalent to the category of finite A^-modules'

proof.text: ($\Gamma_\bullet$ is an equivalence.) Fully faithful: for quasi-coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ on $X$ the map $\alpha\mapsto\Gamma(X,\alpha)$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Gamma(X,\mathcal F),\Gamma(X,\mathcal G))$, is bijective: it is the composite of the bijection given by the counit isomorphism $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}:\widetilde{\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)}\cong\mathcal F$ ((3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]) and the adjunction bijection (1) there (naturality of the adjunction). Hence a family $(\alpha_n)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps commutes with the transition maps iff the $\Gamma(X,\alpha_n)$ do, and $\Gamma_\bullet$ is bijective on morphisms. Essentially surjective, with the explicit quasi-inverse $(M_n)\mapsto(\widetilde{M_n})$: given $(M_n)$ in $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A,I}$, $\widetilde{M_n}$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] with $\Gamma(X,\widetilde{M_n})\cong M_n$ via $\tau_X$ ([lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (2)), so it is of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a), hence coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; the transition maps are $\widetilde{(\cdot)}$ of those of $(M_n)$ (functoriality, (1) there). By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1),(2), $\mathcal I^n\widetilde{M_n}$ is quasi-coherent with global sections $I^nM_n=0$, so it is $0$ (counit isomorphism (3)), and the map $\widetilde{M_{n+1}}/\mathcal I^n\widetilde{M_{n+1}}\to\widetilde{M_n}$ is a map of quasi-coherent modules which on global sections is $M_{n+1}/I^nM_{n+1}\to M_n$, an isomorphism, hence an isomorphism (fully faithfulness just shown). So $(\widetilde{M_n})\in\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ and $\tau_X$ gives $\Gamma_\bullet((\widetilde{M_n}))\cong(M_n)$ naturally. A fully faithful essentially surjective functor is an equivalence; a quasi-inverse is $(M_n)\mapsto(\widetilde{M_n})$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087W, first sentence (the reduction via Lemma 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; Schemes, Lemmas 01I7, 01IA, 01IB for the equivalence of quasi-coherent modules on Spec A with A-modules); the verification is written out by the agent

proof.text: (Generators by Nakayama.) Let $(M_n)\in\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A,I}$ and $M=\varprojlim_nM_n$, an $A^\wedge$-module by $(a_n)_n(x_n)_n=(a_nx_n)_n$, where $A^\wedge=\varprojlim A/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Each transition map is surjective (it induces $M_{n+1}/I^nM_{n+1}\cong M_n$); by induction on $m$, for $m\ge n$ the composite $M_m\to M_n$ is surjective and induces $M_m/I^nM_m\cong M_n$ (as $I^{m-1}\subseteq I^n$). By [lem-weil-pbc-tower-limit-exact-surjective-kernels] (a) every projection $p_n:M\to M_n$ is surjective. Pick $x_1,\dots,x_t\in M$ whose images generate the finitely generated $A$-module $M_1$, and let $\varphi_n:(A/I^n)^{\oplus t}\to M_n$ send the $i$-th basis vector to $p_n(x_i)$; the $\varphi_n$ form a morphism of inverse systems. Each $\varphi_n$ is surjective: $M_n$ is a module over $R=A/I^n$, the ideal $I/I^n$ of $R$ is nilpotent ($(I/I^n)^n=0$), and $M_n/IM_n\cong M_1$ is generated by the images of the $p_n(x_i)$, i.e. $M_n=\varphi_n(R^{\oplus t})+IM_n$; so $\varphi_n$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087W: 'As the transition maps are surjective, we see that M -> M_1 is surjective. Pick x_1, ..., x_t in M which map to generators of M_1. This induces a map of systems (A/I^n)^t -> M_n. By Nakayama's lemma (Algebra, Lemma 00DV, lemma-NAK) these maps are surjective'

proof.text: (The kernels and Mittag-Leffler.) Let $K_n=\operatorname{Ker}\varphi_n\subseteq(A/I^n)^{\oplus t}$; $(K_n)$ is an inverse system (sub-system of $((A/I^n)^{\oplus t})$). Its transition maps are surjective: let $k\in K_n$ and $y\in(A/I^{n+1})^{\oplus t}$ a lift. Then $\varphi_{n+1}(y)$ lies in the kernel of $M_{n+1}\to M_n$, which is $I^nM_{n+1}=\varphi_{n+1}(I^n(A/I^{n+1})^{\oplus t})$ ($\varphi_{n+1}$ is surjective, step 3); choose $z\in I^n(A/I^{n+1})^{\oplus t}$ with $\varphi_{n+1}(z)=\varphi_{n+1}(y)$; then $y-z\in K_{n+1}$ maps to $k$, as $z$ maps to $0$ in $(A/I^n)^{\oplus t}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tower-limit-exact-surjective-kernels] (b) (over $R=A$) to $0\to K_n\to(A/I^n)^{\oplus t}\xrightarrow{\varphi_n}M_n\to0$: with $K=\varprojlim K_n$ the sequence $0\to K\to\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)^{\oplus t}\to M\to0$ is exact. Now $\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)^{\oplus t}=(A^\wedge)^{\oplus t}$ (limits commute with finite direct sums, coordinatewise), and the map $\varprojlim\varphi_n:(A^\wedge)^{\oplus t}\to M$ is $(a_1,\dots,a_t)\mapsto\sum_ia_ix_i$, which is $A^\wedge$-linear for the module structure of step 3 (componentwise computation). Hence $x_1,\dots,x_t$ generate $M$ over $A^\wedge$, and $M$ is a finitely generated $A^\wedge$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087W: 'Let K_n be the kernel. Property (2) implies that K_{n+1} -> K_n is surjective, in particular the system (K_n) satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition. By Homology, Lemma 02N1 (homology-lemma-Mittag-Leffler) we obtain an exact sequence 0 -> K -> (A^)^t -> M -> 0 with K = lim K_n. Hence M is a finite A^-module.'

proof.text: ($M/I^nM=M_n$.) Fix $n$. The projection $\pi_n:(A^\wedge)^{\oplus t}\to(A/I^n)^{\oplus t}$ is surjective with kernel $I^n(A^\wedge)^{\oplus t}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] (2) for the $A$-module $A$ ($I$ is finitely generated as $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), coordinatewise. Since $p_n\circ\varprojlim\varphi=\varphi_n\circ\pi_n$ and both $\pi_n,\varphi_n$ are surjective, $p_n$ is surjective (also step 3). As $I^nM_n=0$, $I^nM\subseteq\operatorname{Ker}p_n$. Conversely let $p_n(m)=0$, $m=\varprojlim\varphi(y)$ with $y\in(A^\wedge)^{\oplus t}$. Then $\pi_n(y)\in K_n$, and the projection $K\to K_n$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-tower-limit-exact-surjective-kernels] (a), so there is $k\in K$ with $\pi_n(k)=\pi_n(y)$; then $y-k\in\operatorname{Ker}\pi_n=I^n(A^\wedge)^{\oplus t}$ and $m=\varprojlim\varphi(y-k)\in I^nM$. So $\operatorname{Ker}p_n=I^nM$, where $I^nM$ (the $A$-submodule generated by the $am$, $a\in I^n$) equals $(IA^\wedge)^nM$. With step 1 applied to $(\mathcal F_n)$ this proves (1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087W, last sentences: 'As K -> K_n is surjective it follows that M/I^nM = Coker(K -> (A/I^n)^t) = (A/I^n)^t/K_n = M_n' (the identification (A^)^t/I^n(A^)^t = (A/I^n)^t is Algebra, Lemma 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated)

proof.text: (The functor $G$ and completeness of finite $A^\wedge$-modules.) For a finitely generated $A^\wedge$-module $N$ put $G(N)=(N/I^nN)_{n\ge1}$ with the canonical surjections, and $G(f)=(f\bmod I^n)_n$ for an $A^\wedge$-linear $f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] (2) (for the $A$-module $A$) $A^\wedge/I^nA^\wedge\cong A/I^n$, so $N/I^nN$ is a finitely generated $A/I^n$-module, hence a finitely generated $A$-module; $I^n(N/I^nN)=0$ and $(N/I^{n+1}N)/I^n(N/I^{n+1}N)=N/I^nN$. So $G:\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A^\wedge)\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A,I}$ is a functor. The ring $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and it is $J$-adically complete for the ideal $J=IA^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]: $J^n=I^nA^\wedge$, and $A^\wedge\to\varprojlim A^\wedge/I^nA^\wedge$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] (1) for the $A$-module $A$. Since $J^nN=I^nN$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] shows that the canonical map $c_N:N\to\varprojlim_nN/I^nN=\varprojlim G(N)$ is bijective; it is $A^\wedge$-linear and natural in $N$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087W ('it suffices to prove that ... M = lim M_n is a finite A^-module and that M/I^nM = M_n': the other half of the equivalence, that a finite A^-module N is lim N/I^nN, is left implicit there; it is Algebra, Lemma 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor) (3) over the Noetherian ring A^ (Lemma 0316) which is complete (Lemma 05GG))

proof.text: (The equivalence.) By steps 3-4, $\varprojlim:\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A,I}\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A^\wedge)$, $(M_n)\mapsto\varprojlim M_n$, $(f_n)\mapsto\varprojlim f_n$ (which is $A^\wedge$-linear, componentwise), is a functor. By step 6 $c:\mathrm{id}\cong\varprojlim\circ G$ is a natural isomorphism, and by step 5 the maps $p_n$ induce isomorphisms $(\varprojlim M_n)/I^n(\varprojlim M_n)\cong M_n$, compatible with the transition maps and natural in $(M_n)$, i.e. a natural isomorphism $G\circ\varprojlim\cong\mathrm{id}$. So $\varprojlim$ is an equivalence with quasi-inverse $G$. By step 2, $E=\varprojlim\circ\Gamma_\bullet$ is a composite of equivalences, hence an equivalence $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A^\wedge)$, with quasi-inverse the composite of $G$ and $(M_n)\mapsto(\widetilde{M_n})$, i.e. $N\mapsto((N/I^nN)^\sim)_{n\ge1}$ with the canonical surjections (tilde of them). This is (2).

lean.statement: theorem coherentFormalModules_affine (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (J : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).IdealSheafData) (hJ : J = Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom)) : ∃ E : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J ≌ ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A) ↦ Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) N), ∃ p : ∀ F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J, (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj (E.functor.obj F).obj) ⟶ F.obj ⋙ moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of A), (∀ F, Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ (p F)))) ∧ (∀ (F G : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) (f : F ⟶ G) (n : ℕ), (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).map (E.functor.map f).hom ≫ (p G).app (op n) = (p F).app (op n) ≫ (moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of A)).map (f.hom.app (op n))) ∧ (∀ (F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) (n : ℕ), Function.Surjective ((p F).app (op n)) ∧ LinearMap.ker ((p F).app (op n)).hom = I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj (E.functor.obj F).obj))) ∧ (∀ (F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) (n : ℕ) (r : AdicCompletion I A) (a : A) (x : (E.functor.obj F).obj), AdicCompletion.evalₐ I (n + 1) r = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)) a → (p F).app (op n) (r • x) = a • (p F).app (op n) x) ∧ Nonempty (E.inverse ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι (IsCoherentFormalModule J) ≅ ObjectProperty.ι (fun N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A) ↦ Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) N) ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A)) ⋙ tilde.functor (CommRingCat.of A) ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor J)
lean.note: The equivalence carries limit cones, naturality, componentwise completed scalar action, and surjective projections with the specified ideal-power kernels. Its inverse is naturally the shared formalCompletionFunctor applied to tilde of the restricted completed module: on an affine this is the canonical tilde quotient system, including its reductions.
